**1. Are the words on the page?** Yes. The FastML post "Yann LeCun's answers from the Reddit AMA" has this question in bold: "What do you think are the biggest applications machine learning will see in the coming decade?" Directly under it is the answer: "Natural language understanding and natural dialog systems. Self-driving cars. Robots (maintenance robots and such)." The post is by Zygmunt Zając, dated 2014-05-26. It says LeCun answered the questions on Reddit on May 15th and that the blog "hand-picked some of his thoughts and grouped them by topic". So it is a third-party blog excerpt of a written Q&A, not LeCun's own post or the Reddit thread. It does quote the question and answer word for word, so the source could fairly be called a reprinted question and answer. Since the candidate is out on part 1 anyway, "coverage only" against a full pass doesn't matter here.

That isn't the chief executive, founder-leader, chair or named chief scientist of the company. Your role history dates his Chief AI Scientist role to about 2018, so the words came about four years before any qualifying role.

- **Part 4 (source)** is met, at least as coverage.
